name: Power and distribution transformers
principle: Transformers couple windings through a magnetic core to change voltage levels at essentially constant power. Oil-filled units (mineral oil, ester or gas-insulated) dominate power ratings, with ONAN/ONAF/OFAF/ODAF cooling stages; dry-type cast-resin units suit fire-sensitive or confined locations. An on-load tap changer (OLTC) regulates the output voltage under load. Losses, sound level and thermal behaviour are standardised in the IEC 60076 series.

process_steps.name: Primary winding energised, core flux established
Tap changer regulates turns ratio, on-load or off-circuit
Cooling system removes load and no-load losses
Gas, pressure and temperature devices protect the unit

suppliers.name: Hitachi Energy
suppliers.product: power, distribution, GIT and dry-type transformers

performance.basis: Hitachi Energy states its power transformer fleet includes more than 20 units of 800 kV UHVDC and more than 500 units in the 735-765 kV AC class

limitations: oil-filled units need fire-risk assessment, bunding and oil handling offshore
harmonic-rich loads and DC bias from converters raise losses, noise and stray heating
advantages: very high reliability and efficiency with decades of service
broad standardised ranges from pole-mounted units to generator step-up blocks
